elements.name: question18
elements.html:
Opening:

 

The current study is testing a new potential medication for autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

In RA, the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own joints, causing inflammation, pain, and joint damage. The study drug is designed to attach to specific immune cells that drive this inflammation. Once attached, it helps these cells interact with other parts of the immune system, which is intended to calm the overactive immune response.

This study is an early first-in-human trial, so the main goal is to assess the safety of the study drug and understand how it behaves in the body.

elements.name: question20
elements.html:
PART A – Single-Dose Group- Currently active

 

Study Drug

If you are eligible and decide to take part, you’ll receive one injection under the skin (subcutaneous) of the study drug on Day 1. There is no placebo in this study.

Schedule

 

Overall, participation in this study lasts roughly 3 to 4 months, though the exact schedule depends on your individual results and follow-up needs.

The study begins with a screening visit, during which various tests will be conducted to determine whether you can safely participate. These include blood tests, a chest x-ray, and a TB (tuberculosis) test.

If you meet the eligibility criteria, you will then come to the study site for your 5 night stay where you will receive the dose of the study drug. Discharge happens quite late in the afternoon (~5PM).

The in-clinic stay would be within 28 days from your screening appointment. Can you please let us know your availability? The clinic can be flexible on the dates, it just needs to happen within a month from your initial appointment (the earlier the better).

 

Following discharge, you will have regular follow-up visits (8 visits in total) over the next 12 weeks. These take place on Days 8, 11, 15, 22, 29, 43, 57 and 85, counting from your dose (Day 1).

 

Some participants may be asked to attend additional follow-up visits for up to 48 weeks (around 11 months) after their dose if certain blood cell levels are still being monitored to ensure they return to the expected range.

elements.name: question21
elements.html:
PART B – Two-Dose Group- Not active

Study Drug

If you are eligible and decide to take part, you’ll receive two injections under the skin (subcutaneous) of the study drug, given one week apart on Day 1 and Day 8. There is no placebo in this study.  

Following your second dose, you will have regular follow-up visits (7 visits in total) over the next 12 weeks. These take place on Days 11, 15, 22, 29, 43, 57 and 85, counting from your first dose (Day 1). (Day 8 is your second dosing visit.)

Some participants may be asked to attend additional follow-up visits for up to 48 weeks (around 11 months) after their first dose if certain blood cell levels are still being monitored to ensure they return to the expected range.

elements.html:
Reimbursement

You will receive reimbursement for taking part in this study. All medication, tests and medical care required as part of the study will be provided to you free of charge.

 

Reimbursement

 Reimbursement compensates for your time, travel expenses, parking and inconvenience.

• $300 for the screening visit,

• $600 for each night you stay in the clinic,

• $300 for each regular follow-up visit

• $300 for additional visit (for example, an X-ray), if required


You will also get a $500 retention bonus at the end of finishing the study.

 

This would be a total of at least $6500, however this may increase depending on the study duration and your follow-up needs.

elements.name: question25
elements.html:
What counts as a conventional synthetic DMARD (csDMARD) for this criterion:

 

  • Methotrexate
  • Sulfasalazine (Salazopyrin)
  • Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil)
  • Leflunomide (Arava)

  • Azathioprine (Imuran) (sometimes used in RA)

     

What does NOT count for csDMARD:

 

  • Biologic DMARDs (e.g., etanercept [Enbrel, Brenzys], adalimumab [Humira, Amgevita, Hadlima, Hyrimoz, Idacio], infliximab [Remicade, Inflectra, Renflexis], rituximab [Mabthera, Mabthera SC, Riximyo, Truxima], abatacept [Orencia, Orencia ClickJect])

  • Targeted synthetic DMARDs (e.g., tofacitinib [Xeljanz], baricitinib [Olumiant], upadacitinib [Rinvoq])

     

Tip for recruiters: To meet this criterion, the participant must have had an inadequate response to at least ONE conventional synthetic DMARDs (csDMARDs).
 

Prior inadequate response to biologics and/or targeted synthetic therapies (e.g., Humira) is acceptable.

 

Examples of prior inadequate response (pt did not tolerate/ had an inadequate response to all below):
• Methotrexate  → Eligible
• Methotrexate + Sulfasalsine→ Eligible

• Methotrexate + luflunomide + Humira→ Eligible 
 •  Humira + another biologic (no csDMARDs)→ Not Eligible

  • DEGENERATIVE joint diseases are ok - this includes osteoarthritis

 

There is a difference between inflammatory joint disease and degenerative joint disease

  • inflammatory joint disease are often autoimmune or infectious in nature, while degenerative disease are due to mechanical stress and wear and tear on joints over time

elements.name: question5
elements.title: What is your current treatment plan for your RA?

elements.name: question6
elements.html:
Required medication for their RA

(the below is required to be eligible)

Participants MUST be using at least one conventional synthetic DMARD at a stable dose for at least 8 weeks prior to baseline and throughout the study

 

  • azathioprine (Imuran)
  • chloroquine (Chlorquin)
  • hydroxychloroquine (plaquenil)
  • leflunomide (Arava)
  • methotrexate
  • sulfasalazine (Salazopyrin)

 

The above can be used alone or in combination.

HOWEVER, please note that the combination of methotrexate and leflunomide is not allowed!

 

Allowed medication for their RA

(the below can be used by participant)

 

  • Oral corticosteroids (if less than 10 mg/day prednisone or equivalent) prednisone/prednisolone brands in Australia include Panafcort, Predsolone, Predsone, Solone, Sone

     

  • Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs - such as ibuprofen [Nurofen, Brufen], meloxicam [Mobic, Moxicam] etc; up to the maximum recommended dose) are permitted if on a stable dose regimen for ≥4 weeks prior to baseline

 

Medication for their RA that are NOT allowed during the study

(usage of the below excludes participant - some of them CAN however wash out of the medication according to the below time-frame and be considered for the study)

 

  • blinatumomab (Blincyto), obinutuzumab (Gazyva), ocrelizumab (Ocrevus), rituximab (Mabthera, Riximyo, Truxima), or ofatumumab (Arzerra for CLL indication; Kesimpta for the MS indication — same molecule, different registered brand and dose form) (any use in the past 12 months is also excluded)

     

  • Treatment with anti-TNFs (e.g., infliximab [Remicade, Inflectra, Renflexis], certolizumab [Cimzia], golimumab [Simponi, Simponi IV], adalimumab [Humira, Amgevita, Hadlima, Hyrimoz, Idacio]), IL-6 inhibitors (e.g., tocilizumab [Actemra, Actemra SC], sarilumab [Kevzara]), etanercept (Enbrel, Brenzys), or abatacept (Orencia, Orencia ClickJect) <8 weeks

     

  • Inhibitors of JAK, Bruton tyrosine kinase, or tyrosine kinase 2, including baricitinib (Olumiant), tofacitinib (Xeljanz), upadacitinib (Rinvoq), filgotinib (Jyseleca), ibrutinib (Imbruvica), or fenebrutinib (investigational, no registered brand) or any investigational agent; current use or any use within 30 days

     

  • Tacrolimus (Prograf), cyclosporin/ciclosporin (Neoral, Sandimmun), or voclosporin (Lupkynis); current use or any use within 30 days

     

  • Cyclophosphamide (Cycloblastin, Endoxan) or a biologic therapy such as, but not limited to, belimumab (Benlysta), ustekinumab (Stelara), anifrolumab (Saphnelo), or secukinumab (Cosentyx), or atacicept (investigational, no registered brand); current use or any use within the past 2 months

     

  • steroid injection into a joint, muscle, or vein in the past 4 weeks

     

  • previous treatment with alkylating agents such as chlorambucil (Leukeran), or with total lymphoid irradiation

 

⚠️ IMPORTANT – MEDICATION REVIEW REQUIRED

Participants currently taking any of the exclusionary medications listed above may still be considered for the study if they wish to discuss their potential eligibility with the study doctor.

Before booking:

 

  1. Send the participant's details to TST (Laura).
  2. The study doctor will contact the participant to discuss their current treatment plan and liaise with their rheumatologist.

  3. Await confirmation from TST before proceeding with a booking.

     

DO NOT BOOK THE PARTICIPANT until this process has been completed and clearance to proceed has been provided.

 

Please explain that if they are found to be eligible for the study, they will need to stop (wash out of) their current medication for approximately 8 weeks before starting the study medication.

✅ ONLY BOOK a screening visit if TST gives you go go ahead after speaking to the study doctor.

Participants cannot have received a live vaccine within 28 days prior to screening and for the duration of the study (or at least 6 months after receiving the study drug!)

 

Examples of live vaccines in Australia:

  • measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine
  • varicella (chickenpox) vaccine
  • herpes zoster (shingles) vaccine
  • yellow fever vaccine
  • rotavirus vaccine
  • BCG vaccine
  • Japanese encephalitis vaccine (Imojev only)
  • oral typhoid vaccine

 

Non-live vaccines are permitted! They can be received anytime.

 

Examples of non-live vaccines:

  • HPV vaccine
  • influenza (flu) vaccine
  • COVID-19 vaccines
  • pneumoccal vaccine
  • etc.
